newsitem.title: POLAND: Espebepe says debt deal delay could cost.
newsitem.headline: Espebepe says debt deal delay could cost.

text.p: Debt-ridden Polish builder Espebepe SA might lose contracts under negotiation due to a Friday decision to put off a creditors meeting on a possible debt write-off, the firm's head said.

Espebepe president Andrzej Hass told Reuters that a court's decision to postpone Friday's meeting on a possible debt write-off to April 14 could cost the firm contracts under negotiation worth about 60 million zlotys.

"We are really pressed by time. I wanted the next meeting on March 24, but creditors did not agree and the judge set April 14....But in the meantime we can lose contracts for 60 million zlotys," Andrzej Hass said.

Hass told Reuters most of the creditors had already suggested they would vote for a debt restructuring deal envisaging a write-off of about 90 percent by large creditors and about 20 percent by smaller ones.
"There is a big hope that they will agree, I had such signals," Hass said.
Espebepe, which has debts of 74.6 million zlotys, is the first Warsaw-listed firm to be endangered by bankruptcy since bourse trade was resumed in 1991.

The decision on the firm was postponed when a court in the northwestern city of Szczecin said the creditors meeting was invalid after some of the participants had failed to send confirmation that they had been notified of the meeting.
Hass said the fate of the agreement depended on Espebepe's biggest creditor, Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA, to which the firm owes 12 million zlotys.
"If Pomorski votes in favour the agreement will be reached," Hass said.

Espebepe, which reported a 52.1-million-zloty net loss in 1996, has said that if the write-off deal comes through and it receives new orders while reducing its workforce by some 300 employees, the firm could break even in 1997.
